title: Bahasa Inggris Fase F · Bertingkat
subject: inggris
description: Past perfect, third conditional, modal passive, inversion, argumentative texts, summarising, survey bias, and formal tone.
topic: Advanced grammar, argumentative and expository texts, critical reading, formal writing (English Fase F)

items.stem: By the time we arrived, the film ___ .
items.explanation: Past perfect (had + past participle) shows the action that happened first in the past: the film started before we arrived.

options: can continue for a long time without harming the environment
uses as many chemicals as possible
items.explanation: Sustainable means able to continue over time without using up or damaging the resources it depends on.

items.stem: Despite ___ tired, she finished her essay.
items.explanation: After the preposition despite, use a noun or a gerund: despite being tired.

items.stem: If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.
items.explanation: Third conditional for an unreal past: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

items.stem: The safety rules must ___ by all visitors.
items.explanation: Passive with a modal: modal + be + past participle.

items.stem: The main purpose of a hortatory exposition text is to ....
options: persuade readers that something should or should not be done
report a past event in order
items.explanation: A hortatory exposition gives arguments and ends with a recommendation, often using should.

items.stem:
Read the text.
Our school should ban single-use plastic in the canteen. Every day, hundreds of plastic cups and straws end up in the bin after a few minutes of use. Some students argue that reusable bottles are inconvenient. However, the canteen could provide water refill stations, which would make bringing a bottle easy. A ban would cut waste and teach habits that last beyond school.
What is the writer's position?
options: The canteen should ban single-use plastic.
Students should bring their own food.
items.explanation: The first sentence states the claim, and the last sentence restates it. The sentence about inconvenience is an opposing view the writer answers.

items.stem:
Read the text again.
Our school should ban single-use plastic in the canteen. Every day, hundreds of plastic cups and straws end up in the bin after a few minutes of use. Some students argue that reusable bottles are inconvenient. However, the canteen could provide water refill stations, which would make bringing a bottle easy. A ban would cut waste and teach habits that last beyond school.
Which sentence is a counterargument that the writer responds to?
options: Some students argue that reusable bottles are inconvenient.
Our school should ban single-use plastic in the canteen.
Hundreds of plastic cups end up in the bin.
items.explanation: A counterargument presents the other side. The writer then answers it with "However, the canteen could provide water refill stations".

items.stem: Not only ___ the exam, but she also got the highest score.
items.explanation: After a negative phrase like not only at the start, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: Not only did she pass ....

items.stem: An online poll on a gaming website finds that 90% of teenagers want longer school holidays. Why is this result weak evidence about all teenagers?
options: The people who answered visit a gaming website, so they may not represent all teenagers.
90% is too high to be real.
items.explanation: This is sampling bias. A reliable survey needs a sample that represents the whole group, not only visitors to one kind of website.

items.stem: You are writing to a university lecturer to ask for a research paper. Which sentence is the most appropriate?
options: I would be grateful if you could send me a copy of your paper.
Hey, can u share ur paper?
items.explanation: Formal emails use polite, indirect requests such as "I would be grateful if you could ..." and full words instead of chat abbreviations.

items.stem:
Read the text.
A river near a big city was once heavily polluted by factory waste and household rubbish. A clean-up programme involving soldiers, residents and local companies removed tonnes of rubbish, and the water became clearer. However, experts warn that the river will stay healthy only if factories treat their waste and households stop dumping rubbish into it.
Which is the best summary?
options: A clean-up improved the river, but lasting success depends on stopping pollution at its source.
Factories are the only cause of pollution.
The river is now completely clean forever.
items.explanation: A good summary keeps the main idea and the key contrast. The text says the clean-up helped, however the river stays healthy only if pollution stops at its sources.
